correctness.rationale: For a full-dimensional Euclidean flag-transitive regular d-polytope d>=2 and a volume-uniform X, compare squared distances to all vertices (equal vertex norms) and slacks to all supporting facet hyperplanes (unit normals, equal inradius). On each characteristic simplex of a complete face flag, the nearest/second-nearest vertex squared-distance difference is s² times barycentric coordinate lambda_v: all comparisons are affine, v is nearest at every simplex vertex and flagged edge-neighbor w is next, with exact gap s² at v and zero at other flag-face centers. Dual argument on ridge-adjacent facets gives slack difference q lambda_F, q>0 at the flagged facet center. Thus U=lambda_v, V=lambda_F have Dirichlet(1,1,d-1) marginal pair on each volume-uniform d-simplex; mixing flag simplex volumes preserves it. This proves survival (1-u-v)^d on nonnegative simplex and zero beyond, beta marginals, covariance -(d+1)^(-2)(d+2)^(-1), correlation -1/d, and joint exponential scaling. Independently simulated 80,000 uniform tetrahedron points, finding normalized means .2514,.2508 and correlation -.3312 versus .25,.25,-1/3; this diagnostic is not the proof.

evidence: General flag-triangulation facts imply uniform simplex barycentric Dirichlet variables only after proving that the two polytope distance order statistics coincide with the vertex and final-facet barycentric coordinates in every chamber.

originality.rationale: Known flag subdivision and Dirichlet coordinates are standard, and an isolated nearest-vertex margin beta marginal may be known; this claim is the *joint primal–dual* law with facet supporting-hyperplane slack and exact negative dependence. Bäsel 2012 computes regular polygon line chords and two-point distances; Kabluchko–Litvak–Zaporozhets 2015 analyze Gaussian directional widths, neither a uniform interior point’s two order-statistic margins. Searches for same normalization and joint dependency returned no dominating prior result, with bibliographic uncertainty retained.
residual_risks: A joint order-statistics theorem under alternative flag/barycentric terminology could be omitted by the search; searched equivalent geometric descriptions.
Standard Coxeter flag facts used without rederiving regularity classification; no claims for semiregular polytopes.
